text:
Alex: Heads-up — nightly perf job flagged a ~25% increase in p95 serving latency across the small-seq workload after last night's merges :warning:
Priya: saw the alert. link to the perf run: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/1905123456
Casey-bot: [CI PERF] Regression detected on main (build 2026-03-17-23:11): p95 +24.8% on small-seq profile. Suspected range: 3 commits.
Miguel: Which merges landed last night? PR list?
Alex: PRs merged: #4132 (kernel-selector heuristics tweak), #4140 (kv-cache refactor), #4145 (docs). Hashes: 7c1a2b3 (4132), a9f4d2e (4140)
Sam: My money is on 4132 — we changed kernel preference ordering for short sequences to try to reduce memory churn. Could affect latency tail.
Priya: I'll start a git-bisect on the perf runner. running: `git bisect start HEAD HEAD~10; git bisect run ./scripts/run_perf.sh --profile small-seq`
Priya: bisect picked 7c1a2b3 as first bad. Reproduces locally on perf harness with same workload.
Alex: good catch. Sam — can you inspect kernel-selector changes in that commit?
Sam: looking... main change is in selector.go: we moved preferFastMatmul for seq_len < 64 ahead of preferSparse. For short sequences it picks matmul kernels that have worse single-thread scheduling causing queuing under concurrency.
Miguel: so root cause: kernel ordering change increased contention at the GPU execution layer for small-seq bursts. Expected to reduce memory but regressed latency.
Priya: CI suggests revert is fastest to unblock rollouts. Options: 1) revert the merge on main and cherry-pick a smaller fix to release branch, 2) hotfix the kernel scheduler to preserve old ordering for concurrency scenarios. Which do we prefer?
Sam: I can push a minimal guard: keep older ordering when concurrent_inflight > N (N=8). Quick to code and unit test. But risk: might be subtle and need perf verification.
Alex: We need production-stable ASAP. Revert on main + hotfix branch for release sounds safest. Then we can iterate on proper selector change in a follow-up.
Miguel: agree. I'll create a revert PR on main for 7c1a2b3 and prepare a release branch backport.
Miguel: commands I'm going to run:
```
# revert on main
git checkout main
git pull origin main
git revert --no-edit 7c1a2b3
git push origin main
# create hotfix release branch
git checkout -b release/1.9.2-hotfix origin/release/1.9.1
git cherry-pick <fix-commit>  # placeholder for the minimal fix if we later choose to cherry-pick instead
git push origin release/1.9.2-hotfix
```
Priya: I'll kick an expedited perf CI against the revert commit and the hotfix branch. Need to ensure p95 returns to baseline and no new regressions pop up.
Casey-bot: [CI RUN] perf-suite (revert) queued on perf-runner-7
QA_Team: we'll schedule verification on dedicated test cluster once CI passes. Plan: run synthetic small-seq load + 15m soak under concurrency 16.
Sam: I'll also add a small guard in a branch (draft) so we have an alternate fix ready: `selector: if inflight > 8 { use legacyOrdering }`
Alex: timeline: revert PR + CI verification in next 60-90 minutes, then create release branch and backport minimal fix if needed. Can we do a canary rollback on hosted within ~2 hours?
Miguel: yes — once the revert is merged and CI green, we'll push a canary rollout to 5% of traffic for hosting and a single pool in Dedicated. rollout plan in console: canary -> 1h metrics check -> 25% -> 2h -> 100%.
Priya: CI results (revert) finished: p95 delta -0.5% vs baseline, p99 unchanged. Looks good.
Casey-bot: [CI PASS] perf-suite revert confirmed.
Alex: merge the revert then. Miguel, proceed with canary deployment when merged.
Miguel: revert merged to main (commit ef3d9b2). Starting canary deploy to hosted 5% now.
QA_Team: canary started. running the soak. sending logs to #support for telemetry.
Sam: Meanwhile I'm opening PR with the guard branch so we can evaluate a safer selector change in a follow-up: PR #4158 (draft) `selector: concurrency-aware ordering`.
Priya: after 45m canary metrics look stable. p95 back to baseline, no CPU/GPU queuing signals.
Alex: proceed to step up rollout to 25% per plan. Keep watch on tail-latency charts and KV cache hit rates.
Miguel: 25% rollout in progress. also creating release/1.9.2-hotfix and will backport either revert or minimal guard depending on risk assessment for customers on the release branch.
Alex: action items recap:
- Miguel: revert merged (done), canary rollout (in progress), create release branch and backport (in progress)
- Priya: perf CI verification and monitoring (done for revert)
- Sam: open PR for guard approach and perf benchmark it (#4158)
- QA_Team: canary soak and regression tests (in progress)
- Alex: coordinate customer comms if rollback affects any rolling updates

Miguel: I'll post final status once release branch is ready and we've decided whether to cherry-pick guard vs full revert backport. Thanks all :thumbsup:
QA_Team: canary soak passed, no regressions observed.
Alex: closing thread once release branch backport is confirmed. Good job everyone — quick detection and revert prevented a bad rollout. :rocket:
